text.p: Hurricane Hortense remains a strong risk to shipping as it moves northward during the next 48-72 hours. It is expected to be well east of the central Bahamas islands tonight, east of the North Carolina coast today and early Saturday and near or over Nova Scotia Canada Sunday. Maximum sustained winds are 140 mph at this time. They should continue at about this level into Friday morning then begin to weaken Friday afternoon.

Hurricane Fausto continues as a major risk to shipping in the region south of and near southern Baja during the next 24 hours. Maximum sustained winds with this system are currently 115 mph. This system is also a major risk to property in southern Baja and in north Sinaloa and south Sonora Mexico. Baja should be hard hit by rains, wind and a coastal storm surge with battering waves within the next 12-24 hours. The impact in Sinaloa and Sonora should be due to flooding rains and mudslides. Landfall in mainland Mexico is about 24-36 hours away.

Tropical storm Tom is mostly a risk to shipping as it tracks north of Saipan with winds of up to 50 mph. The system will likely track near Agrihan in the northern Mariana Islands over the next 12-18 hours. Some of this area may see property damage due to winds and flooding rains. This system continues to strengthen as it moves west of the Mariana islands thereafter.
Tropical depression 24w is a minor risk to shipping and coastal property in central Vietnam as it drifts into the Gulf of Tonkin very poorly organized.
Tropical Storm Violet is mainly a threat to shipping as it strengthens in the Philippine Sea. This system will move very little over the next 24 hours.
